newsitem.title: GERMANY: Euro banknote designs to be unveiled on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Euro banknote designs to be unveiled on Friday.

text.p: Europe's planned single currency, the Euro, is set to lose part of its mystery on Friday when the European Monetary Institute unveils the designs for the banknotes which should be filling European wallets from 2002.

European leaders attending this week's European Council meeting in Dublin will get the first glimpse of the designs which won a contest launched in February by the EMI, the forerunner to the European Central Bank.
The public unveiling will follow immediately after, with news conferences planned for both Dublin and the EMI's headquarters in Frankfurt at 1400 GMT.
There will be seven designs in all, one for each of the denominations in the planned banknote series -- Euro 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 500.

The decision on designs at this early stage, with two years to go to the planned Euro launch in 1999, will ensure that the banknotes can be put into circulation toward the end of 2001, or start of 2002 at the latest, the EMI has said.
The competition to design the Euro opened in February and closed on September 13.
Contenders -- only experienced banknote designers approved by a national central bank could apply -- were invited to choose between specific traditional or contemporary design models.

The traditional option for example -- based on the theme "Ages and Styles in Europe" -- was required to have a feature such as a portrait representing a period on one side of the note and an architectural feature from the same period on the other.
The EMI also said the designs would have to allow for "a number of advanced security features" to prevent forgeries.
